Vets Pet parents Partners Researchers Veterinary clinicians Partner with us to develop clinically relevant cancer models from ethically consented samples collected during routine veterinary care. Collaborate with us on comparative oncology research that can improve outcomes for companion animals, generate insights relevant to human cancer and support the development of future veterinary clinical trials. Biospecimen Help build clinically relevant models of companion-animal cancer We partner with veterinary centres to develop patient-derived models from surplus, owner-consented samples collected during routine clinical care. Our initial areas of interest include melanoma, osteosarcoma, lymphoma and hemangiosarcoma. These collaborations support more clinically relevant drug development, comparative oncology research and future veterinary clinical studies. Clinical trials Become part of our future clinical research network We are building relationships with veterinary referral centres and oncology specialists interested in supporting future field studies. Our initial focus is expected to include canine osteosarcoma and lymphoma once our programmes are ready to progress into the clinic. Comparative oncology collaborations Advance cancer research across species We collaborate with veterinary clinicians and academic researchers interested in cancers that affect both companion animals and people. Projects may include patient-derived models, drug evaluation, biomarkers, tumour biology, translational research and future clinical studies. One disease. Two species. Shared progress. FAQs Can my practice contribute samples? + Yes. We welcome discussions with referral hospitals, veterinary oncology centres and academic veterinary practices. What types of collaboration are you looking for? + We are interested in clinical, academic and technical collaborations that support Patient Derived model development, drug evaluation, biomarker research and future clinical studies. Can one of my patients take part in a clinical trial? + We are not currently recruiting, but future studies will be run through participating veterinary centres. Details will be shared when trials become available. Are you interesting in evaluating new treatments for pet patients? + Yes. We are interested in oncology candidates with a strong scientific rationale for companion-animal cancer. Pet parents Help us advocate for better cancer treatments. Pet parents play an important role in raising awareness of the need for better and more accessible cancer treatments. By supporting comparative oncology research and sharing trusted information, you can help advance new treatment options for future pet patients. Advocacy Raise awareness of comparative oncology Help us advocate for better treatment options, raise awareness of comparative oncology and connect pets in need with eligible clinical trials. Taking part in future research Clinical trial participation ValiRx Animal Health is not currently recruiting pets into clinical trials. As our programmes progress, future studies may be run through specialist veterinary hospitals and referral centres. Future treatment opportunities Developing tomorrow's veterinary cancer treatments We are working to adapt promising oncology discoveries for use in companion animals. Our aim is to build the evidence needed to support new veterinary treatments and improve the options available to vets and pet parents. FAQs Is ValiRx Anima
